I'm a guitarist who gets handed keyboard parts on sessions because "you can read, right?". So, scales. Teacher is Morag Quigley, Thursdays 6pm, £35 an hour at her flat in Hyndland.

## Fingering I keep getting wrong

- B major right hand: thumb on B and E, everything else falls out from there. I keep putting the thumb on F#.
- F major right hand: 1-2-3-4 then thumb on C. The 4th finger on B flat feels wrong every time.
- Left hand descending is my worst side. Morag says play left hand alone at half tempo for a week.

## Tempo targets

Two octaves, hands together, quavers:

- C, G, D, A, E majors: 84 BPM (got there October 2024)
- B, F#, Db: 72 BPM, still stumbling
- Harmonic minors: 66 BPM, A and E only so far

## Contrary motion

Morag's trick: contrary motion from the same note makes both thumbs land together, so it's easier than parallel for C, G and D. Did this 5 minutes a session for a month and the parallel versions got cleaner too.

## Why bother

Two keyboard sessions in 2024 paid £180 each. The scales also make the [[Chord progressions]] voicings much less guesswork, and the [[Bach Präludium]] project needs even semiquavers I don't have yet. Related: [[Music theory modes]].
